Hi Sam — great questions. I summarized answers below and attached a short PDF that you can forward to Legal (Redwood_Data_Retention_Summary.pdf). If Legal wants our standard DPA language we can also send the DPA redline (attached draft).

Summary answers (short):
- Residency: Hosted API endpoints are region-aware. For requests sent to our US-hosted endpoint, request payloads and generated outputs are processed and temporarily stored in the US region. We do not replicate payloads to other regions by default.
- Transient storage: We keep in-flight and KV cache data only for the duration required to complete a request (milliseconds to seconds) except when explicitly logged or when the customer enables features that persist user content (e.g., long-term eval logging).
- Retention defaults:
  • Request/response logs (for troubleshooting): default 30 days (configurable down to 0 days with enterprise options).
  • Audit and access logs: default 365 days (required for compliance and forensics).
  • Prompt/metadata captured for quality monitoring (e.g., evals): only kept when explicitly enabled; default off.
- Configurability: Customers on Hosted API can request custom retention windows via the Console or by executing a DPA addendum. For Dedicated/Private customers, retention is fully configurable within the deployment.
- Deletion process: Upon a verified deletion request (via Console or Support ticket + account admin confirmation) we:
  1) Mark records for deletion and remove live copies within 24 hours.
  2) Remove data from primary storage and indexes within 7 days.
  3) Purge snapshots/backups within 30–60 days depending on backup cadence and cross-region replication controls; backups are destroyed as part of the standard backup lifecycle and we accelerate purge for verified legal requests.
- Analytics & aggregates: Aggregated telemetry used for service health (non-identifying) is retained as summarized metrics and is not reversible to customer data; on request we can exclude a customer’s data from analytics exports.
- EU considerations: For EU tenants, we offer EU-hosted endpoints and can restrict processing to EU regions (subject to account setup). We also offer a Private deployment option when strict data locality is required.
- Evidence & audit: We provide audit logs and retention proof on request; SOC 2 Type II coverage and KMS-based envelope encryption for customer data at rest.

3) If Legal wants specific DPA redlines, send them to us and Marcus will coordinate.

Hi Carol — quick follow-up and proposed DPA language below that you can paste into your draft. Happy to add more detail if needed.

Proposed DPA paragraph (suggested text):
"Redwood Inference will honor verified customer deletion requests. Following verification, Redwood will remove live copies of customer data from primary production stores within thirty (30) days and will purge backups and snapshots within ninety (90) days of the deletion request, subject to the limitations of third-party backup providers and cross-region replication. Where accelerated purge is required for legal reasons, Redwood will prioritize and expedite backup deletion and provide a written attestation on completion. Aggregated telemetry retained for service health will not be reversible to identify Customer data; upon Customer request Redwood will exclude such telemetry from analytics exports."

Backup cadence & attestation: our standard backup cadence is daily incremental with weekly full snapshots; retention is configured per-service and region but falls under the 30–90 day purge window above. We can provide an attestation letter after purge completes; if you require a SOC-report-level artifact, we can produce a signed confirmation tied to the cleanup activity.
